thread:
sarah: Thanks everyone for the live Qs — posting a follow-up thread for engineering process items (shipping rhythm, on-call updates, quality gates, SLAs). Ask specifics and I'll answer. cc @ops-bot for links
ajay: Quick one — what's the new shipping tempo for minor fixes vs feature launches? trying to plan roadmap.
linda: Also, are we changing the on-call rotations? last week's overlap was rough.
sarah: Short answers: minor patches get a weekly ship window, regular feature releases go through a monthly stable window, and major platform releases are quarterly. We keep an emergency hotfix flow. Canary runs for 48h, then gradual rollout if no regressions.
mike: For Dedicated customers, what SLA numbers are we targeting? 99.9 or 99.95?
sarah: Dedicated: target SLA 99.95% uptime on a monthly rolling window. Hosted remains best-effort with published SLOs in Console. We'll publish error budgets and the escalation playbook next week.
rachel: On quality bars — what counts as a blocking regression during rollout? unit test failures vs perf regressions?
oliver: And for perf, do we gate on p50 or p99 token latencies?
sarah: Blocking = anything that meaningfully increases end-user errors or breaks correctness tests on canary. For perf, p50 is informative, but p95/p99 are the safety gates for rollout decisions. We'll add this checklist to the PR/release template.
ajay: Can you paste a short checklist snippet? even a minimal one helps planners.
ops-bot: https://redwood.example.com/processes/releases — release playbook and rollout checklist
sarah: Snippet:
```
- Run canary for 48h
- Monitor p95/p99 latency and error budget consumption
- Run smoke tests + core integration tests
- Confirm rollback plan and tag release
```
linda: Will infra on-call headcount change? we had only two people last rotation and it felt thin.
sarah: We're adding one more infra on-call for the next two quarters and shifting to a 4-day rotation to reduce fatigue. Ops handover doc will be updated with escalation contacts.
mike: How will teams be notified about SLA burn — Slack alerts, Console, email?
sarah: Both. Console dashboards + automated Slack alerts that tag owners when thresholds hit. We'll pilot a weekly SLA email digest for product owners.
rachel: Any change to expectations around PR size / long-running branches? last time big PRs caused integration regressions.
sarah: We want smaller, decoupled PRs. We'll add a 'long-running-pr' flag in GitHub and require an explicit rollback plan if a PR is open >5 days.
ajay: Thanks, really helpful. One more — are we formalizing release freezes for major holidays?
sarah: Yes. We'll publish a holiday freeze calendar. Generally no major releases during core business holidays; patches OK with on-call signoff.
oliver: :thumbsup: I can help draft the PR template updates if useful.
sarah: Please do, @oliver — assign the draft to me and I'll review. Closing thread with action items.
